scope: Exactly three privately owned16KiB root/leaf/data IOBufferMemoryDescriptor allocations, actual descriptor retention and explicit preparation pairs, integrating frozen private_lifecycle without changing it. No IOMapper publication, MMIO, DART programming, IRQ, firmware, activation, packet or boot.

pinned_API_facts.factory: IOBufferMemoryDescriptor.h:264-268 declares static OSPtr<IOBufferMemoryDescriptor> inTaskWithPhysicalMask(task_t,IOOptionBits,mach_vm_size_t,mach_vm_address_t). cpp:564-575 passes alignment1 to initWithPhysicalMask and resets a failed construction.
pinned_API_facts.smart_pointer_mode: OSPtr.h:34-88 selects OSSharedPtr only with IOKIT_ENABLE_SHARED_PTR, C++17+, and IOKIT_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_SHARED_PTR_IN_API when not PRIVATE. The proposed native TU opts into these explicitly before headers; future compile fixture must verify the actual return type rather than assume default raw-pointer mode.
pinned_API_facts.mask: IOBufferMemoryDescriptor.cpp:243-263 skips gSystem with MapperNone; mask handling only when supplied alignment<=1. It derives alignment=((mask^(-1ULL))&(mask-1))+1 and highestMask=mask|lowbits, then raises alignment to current page_size.
pinned_API_facts.allocation: cpp:315-347 nonpageable allocation is wired, internally ORs AutoPrepare, and HostPhysicallyContiguous forces physical contiguity. super initialization cpp:445-451 receives system-mapper NULL but MapperNone prevents actual automatic mapping. IOMemoryDescriptor.cpp:2466-2468 invokes constructor auto-prepare.
pinned_API_facts.owned_pair: IOMemoryDescriptor.h:750-764 prepare/complete must be paired and serialized. cpp:4437-4480 validates direction even when already wired; prepare cpp:5024-5071 increments wire count only on success; complete cpp:5084-5185 processes/decrements count. The native provider tracks its own one explicit pair separately from constructor-internal ownership, never reads private wire-count fields.
pinned_API_facts.query: IOBufferMemoryDescriptor.h:301-342 exposes getCapacity and getBytesNoCopy; initial length equals capacity. IOMemoryDescriptor.h:425-435 getPhysicalSegment(offset,&length,options) and cpp:3694-3719 use kIOMemoryMapperNone for source physical rather than mapped addresses. A CPU pointer, PA or physical-mask argument alone is not ownership proof.
pinned_API_facts.free: IOBufferMemoryDescriptor.cpp:705-795 calls super::free before freeing associated allocation; IOMemoryDescriptor.cpp:2482-2500 may complete outstanding wire references during free. Releasing the last real descriptor can therefore complete/unwire/free backing. Core metadata retirement does none of this.

restrictions: Require actual native CPU page_size/PAGE_SIZE to be0x4000 before allocation in this initial profile; no assumption from target triple. Mask still explicitly imposes16KiB alignment independently of the usual current-page-size default.
Use the static physical-mask factory so alignment argument is1. Do not call initWithPhysicalMask with explicit alignment0x4000 and assume the physical mask is applied.
No Pageable/Purgeable/user-sharing/cache-override/HostOnly/automatic mapper options; retain ordinary wired kernel backing. HostPhysicallyContiguous is explicit for one16KiB object.

No allocation argument represents an IOVA or hardware DMA authority. MapperNone is for private backing allocation/source-PA enumeration, not device bypass. Every actual full span still requires trusted RAM/reservation validation.

Allocation may block. No allocation, prepare, physical query, complete or last-reference reset at interrupt level, under a simple lock or while holding the short registry/provider mutex. No device or system mapper is invoked intentionally.

boot_lifetime_anchor.ownership: One canonical platform-domain anchor, retained by a boot-lifetime owner independent of any provider/service start result, caller stack, autorelease pool or provider member destructor. It owns a stable four-job array and the one initialized frozen core registry. Root domain creation must prevent duplicate anchors/registries for the same domain.
boot_lifetime_anchor.allocation_transfer: Pre-reserve the job/lease/anchor slot first. For each role assign the factory OSPtr result directly into its empty anchored descriptor field, or perform an immediate verified move before any explicit prepare/query/copy or failure-return branch. No local RAII sole owner may survive into an uncertain native operation. Returned nonnull reference is owned exactly once by the anchor; avoid both extra retain leaks and unretained adoption.
boot_lifetime_anchor.failure_lifetime: The anchor remains alive if provider start fails, caller drops its token or an enclosing provider object is freed. QUARANTINED and IN_PROGRESS jobs retain actual descriptors plus claims until reboot. A normal local destructor is never the retention mechanism. Never clear/reset/replace an anchored live field on error.
boot_lifetime_anchor.unload: No module unload or anchor destruction while any native call, live claim, retained backing, quarantined job or recorded exposure exists. The initial implementation offers no unload/drain/force-release escape. A service free path must not trigger automatic descriptor-member destruction; it can discard only a facade reference while the independent anchor remains.
job_fields: anchor identity and core registry identity
provider job generation and monotonic nonzero per-descriptor handle/generation (no reuse/wrap)
phase, busy owner/op sequence, first error, ever_exposed
per-role own prepare started/returned/result and owns_prepare_pair
per-role own complete started/returned/result and own_pair_balanced
validated CPU address, PA, physical span length, length/capacity
boot_lifetime_anchor.factory_boundary_limit: The caller cannot anchor an object before the native factory returns it: constructor-internal allocation/AutoPrepare/failure cleanup remain the pinned XNU implementation responsibility. A returned nonnull OSPtr is anchored before any provider explicit prepare; a known NULL return is a factory refusal, not permission to guess a preparation pair. A nonreturn/unknown factory call keeps job/claims in progress, never starts a retry or claims its hidden native storage was reclaimed. This design does not claim control over an unreturned constructor-internal object.

proposed_internal_API.status: Design signatures/semantics only, no implementation or permission to execute.
proposed_internal_API.create_domain_anchor: Create canonical root-owned boot-lifetime anchor with fixed trusted policy, zero registry -> bpl_init once. No current hardware access or IOService publication.
proposed_internal_API.acquire_private(request,data_iova,data_p: Under short domain lock reserve one job, call bpl_claim, snapshot trusted policy, mark operation busy. Then synchronous native allocation/preparation/validation outside lock. Return only PRIVATE_BACKING_VALIDATED (not DMA_READY) and opaque anchor/job/generation token on full success.
proposed_internal_API.zero_private(token): Only private/unexposed validated job, recheck exact token/core snapshot and owned refs; zero exactly all3 verified16KiB CPU buffers. No hardware/table-publication state transition.
proposed_internal_API.copy_private_data(token,offset,source,le: Only initialized, private/unexposed validated job; checked offset+length<=0x4000 and bounded nonzero accessible immutable source disjoint from anchor/registry/owned buffers. Copy data role only. No firmware semantic interpretation, root/leaf arbitrary-write API or raw borrowed pointer escape.
proposed_internal_API.inspect(token,out_snapshot): Copy bounded metadata/counters only under short lock, no descriptor getters or native I/O during inspection. No returned retainable descriptor/CPU-view capability.
proposed_internal_API.retire_private(token): Synchronous state machine described below; only method allowed to attempt owned complete pairs and metadata retirement. No retry on pending/uncertain/quarantined call.

acquisition_sequence.action: Validate trusted policy and request before side effects: native16KiB page size, exactly one canonical domain registry, finite RID/SID/vector numeric request, proposed data IOVA aligned/in codec aperture, permissions R/W only; checked job/handle/generation limits. bpl_claim holds metadata resource reservations, not hardware authority.

Set domain operation busy under mutex, retain anchor independently, then release short mutex. Native allocation calls execute in root/leaf/data order at most once each; mark allocation-start before each and transfer each nonnull returned OSPtr directly into anchor before next step. No explicit prepare until every returned reference is anchored. Refuse unexpected duplicate descriptor identity without trying to repair ownership.

For each descriptor, mark own prepare IN_PROGRESS before one prepare(kIODirectionOutIn); only KERN/kIOReturnSuccess marks owned pair=1 and prepare-returned-success. Constructor AutoPrepare is a separate native baseline; omitting private AutoPrepare option never suppressed it. Any non-success, exception boundary, stale operation result, interrupted/unknown outcome or still-running call quarantines all anchored refs and the core lease; no compensating complete or retry.

After all3 own prepares succeeded, query actual getLength()==0x4000 and getCapacity()==0x4000; getBytesNoCopy nonnull/aligned16KiB; getPhysicalSegment(0,&spanLength,kIOMemoryMapperNone) must supply a complete contiguous aligned16KiB PA extent. Do not call getPhysicalAddress alone or infer contiguity/high bits from allocator options. Store actual validated facts in anchored records.

Before provider zero/copy, independently validate every CPU/PA checked half-open extent, PA<2^36 including last byte, exact trusted full-page RAM membership and reserved exclusion. Check three descriptors/handles and CPU+PA pages mutually distinct, no overlap with registry/anchor/control/scratch/source storage, no conflicts with every other anchored live/quarantined job. If physical/control ownership policy input is unavailable, refuse rather than make a success-shaped span. Constructor/allocator-internal initialization is distinct from provider zero/copy.

Build exactly3 bpl_span values from the actual anchored records: root/leaf roles permissions0/iova0; data explicit R/W and checked numeric data_iova reservation. handle/generation are provider identities linked to real refs, not caller-fabricated pointer numbers. bpl_bind_metadata must succeed once, before any effect journal entry. Core numerical acceptance supplements but cannot authenticate native ownership. A known validation/bind refusal takes private cleanup only if every own native pair outcome is known.

After acquire returns PRIVATE_BACKING_VALIDATED, zero_private may transition to PRIVATE_INITIALIZED by zeroing exactly all3 verified16KiB buffers. Only then may bounded copy_private_data run. These remain private CPU writes; root/leaf stay zero in this slice. No table encoding/install or hardware graph claim. Recheck token/private core state before each operation; no bus-address/hardware-ready result.

core_integration_rules.unchanged_core: Use frozen c585/00ae/87d4 as linked pure C core; no structure mutation, copy/reset/reinit, forced state transition or alternate private-retire helper.
core_integration_rules.claim_retention: Keep exact live lease and all native refs while allocation/preparation/query/private initialization/completion is in progress. A bpl_span is numeric metadata, never substitute for an actual retained descriptor.
core_integration_rules.journal_boundary: This source slice performs only CPU-private allocation, preparation, source-PA queries and CPU writes with MapperNone; none is a hardware config/mapping/descriptor/producer/doorbell/IRQ effect. It invokes no bpl_effect_begin as a substitute for real provider ownership. All actual exposure APIs are absent. Any future external effect must be designed/reviewed separately, bind actual backing first, and journal before its external call.
core_integration_rules.unexpected_history: If inspection finds pending/effect_count/ever_resources, EFFECT_RECORDED or QUARANTINED, private retirement is prohibited immediately. Retain all refs and claims; never complete/free via this private-only API, even if a recorded effect said success/no-op.
core_integration_rules.IOVA_scope: data_iova is an exclusive numeric private reservation checked by core, not a real IOMapper allocation or programmed translation. No hardware or mapper bypass follows.
core_integration_rules.policy_scope: Core trusted domain labels and caller RAM/reservation lists are not discovery or physical exclusivity. Canonical anchor creation and actual provider provenance remain trusted platform obligations.
core_integration_rules.C_CPP_linkage: Frozen lifecycle.h has no __cplusplus extern-C guards. Do not edit it. Future C++ provider includes it inside an explicit extern "C" wrapper or a separate bridge header; lifecycle.c remains compiled as C. Mixed-language link must resolve unmangled bpl_* symbols.

retirement_sequence_critical.action: Validate exact token and not-busy private job, then bpl_inspect under short lock. Require CLAIMED or PRIVATE_METADATA, pending0/effect_count0/ever_resources0, no quarantine/exposure or uncertain native operation. Set RETIRING/busy, keep core lease LIVE and all descriptors strongly retained.

Outside short lock, for each role with its own prepare-success/unbalanced pair, record COMPLETE_IN_PROGRESS before exactly one complete(kIODirectionOutIn) in reverse order (data,leaf,root). Descriptor must remain in anchor throughout; no OSPtr reset/release yet. A record with no own prepare ever attempted needs no own complete. Never consume constructor AutoPrepare baseline explicitly.

Only known success balances that one own pair. On the FIRST non-success/unknown/hang/stale result: stop native cleanup, bpl_quarantine with first error when exact lease still valid, retain all3 refs and all claims until reboot. Do not retry failed/pending complete, do not complete later records, and do not release even earlier successfully completed descriptors. If exact lease identity cannot be established, retain orphaned native job without mutating another core owner.

After EVERY needed own completion succeeded, reacquire lock and verify busy token/private history still unchanged. ONLY NOW call bpl_retire_private. If it fails, retain/quarantine refs; no reset. Successful metadata retirement marks CORE_RETIRED_REFS_RETAINED, not FREE or backing-released.

Keep domain operation exclusivity and anchor lifetime while clearing internal CPU views and separately resetting the3 native descriptor refs. No untrusted callback can obtain them. Native reset/release has no IOReturn; record only invocation/return, not a hardware drain/physical free attestation. Constructor-owned AutoPrepare cleanup belongs to native destruction; there is no provider loop calling complete until success.

Only after all native reference-reset calls returned and fields are empty may provider mark PRIVATE_REFS_RELEASED, clear busy and make its job storage reusable under a new nonwrapping generation. bpl lease is already invalid. A crash/hang/unknown last-release state never reuses the anchor/job or advertises actual release.

failure_matrix.case: Invalid request/core claim rejected before native call
failure_matrix.action: No descriptor acquired; no new native complete/release. Preserve outputs. Return finite refusal.

failure_matrix.case: Factory returned NULL with no own prepare attempted anywhere
failure_matrix.action: Known allocation refusal; retain any earlier returned refs until private metadata retirement succeeds, then reset those private native refs. No own complete calls. Unknown/not-returned allocation remains busy/anchored and is never retried concurrently.

failure_matrix.case: Known post-prepare length/PA/policy/bind validation failure, all native prepare outcomes known
failure_matrix.action: Run the exact ordered private-complete sequence with live core claims. Only all needed completions success -> core retirement -> separate native resets. Any cleanup uncertainty takes quarantine instead.
No compensating complete because ownership of that pair is uncertain. Quarantine actual entire cohort+claims until reboot; bounded leak intentionally preferred to guessing pair count.

failure_matrix.case: Some completes succeeded then another failed/unknown
failure_matrix.action: Keep earlier completed descriptors retained too. Unattempted own pairs stay outstanding; failed pair is uncertain. No retry, continuation or core retirement.
Private completion/retirement/ref reset forbidden; keep real refs and core history. This slice has no after-exposure cleanup API.

failure_matrix.case: Provider/start/free/unload failure or caller token drop
failure_matrix.action: Independent boot anchor remains owner; no stack/member destructor releases uncertain state. No hidden destructor cleanup. Unload/free remains blocked while retained job exists.

serialization_and_reentry.short_mutex: One domain sleeping mutex protects registry, job phases and immutable record publication. Core calls are callback-free and can run inside this short critical section. Never hold it over blocking native allocation/prepare/complete/last-ref reset.
serialization_and_reentry.busy_protocol: Before dropping mutex mark exact job and domain operation busy with monotonic op identity. Other threads or same-thread native-callback reentry observe BUSY and return without claims/native actions; they do not wait for themselves or start cleanup. Inspection may copy bounded snapshots only.
serialization_and_reentry.return_identity: On native return reacquire mutex and match anchor/job/core generation plus in-progress operation. Stale, duplicated or out-of-order results cannot act on a reused job and cause retained failure for the actual in-progress owner.
serialization_and_reentry.timeout: No worker timeout may cancel a native call and free/reuse its job. Still-running calls retain anchor/refs/claims and exclude a second cleanup caller. Native blocking latency has no new wallclock proof in this design.
serialization_and_reentry.external_registry_callers: All platform core users must obey the same domain-operation serialization; a parallel direct bpl_claim/retire caller bypassing it violates this design. No promise of thread safety from raw exposed C structs.

future_host_fixture_requirements: Use actual unchanged lifecycle.c with an original injectable provider-op boundary that models descriptor objects/ref ownership, ctor auto-prepare baseline and exactly one explicit pair separately. Host fake pages are not native IOBuffer/DMA proof.

Trace acquire-ref/move-to-anchor before prepare-start; a returned object must remain anchored after every injected prepare/complete failure, late/unknown return, facade destruction, start failure and reentry. Count actual fake refs, not just core state booleans.

Fault every allocation/own-prepare/query/validation/bind/complete/core-retire/reset boundary. Positive traces require claims LIVE during every complete; all completes known-success strictly precede bpl_retire_private; actual refs reset strictly follow it. Reject complete-after-retire and partial-complete-then-free mutants.

Simulate prepare failing before or after native state mutation; complete failing before/after decrement; no result/duplicate/stale result. Unknown cases must never retry/guess pair count, retire core or release actual refs. Refusal remains until reboot in that fixture, not a forced reset test path.

Test exact3 roles, full16KiB lengths/capacities, 36-bit last-page boundary, alignment, zero/noncontiguous/short spans, CPU/PA/handle duplicates, self/registry/control overlaps, reserved holes, unavailable/truncated policy, bad IOVA/permissions and cross-job collisions. No provider zero/copy before all full-span/policy/core checks.

Check actual selected mask math0xfffffc000 -> align0x4000/highest0xfffffffff and native call arguments/option set; reject all36ones-as-explicit-alignment substitute and direct-init(mask,alignment>1) mutants. No system mapper/default page-size assumption.

Reentry from each native callback must return BUSY with no second call; two simultaneous operations cannot mutate one registry. Do not hold the mutex during native callbacks. Concurrent inspect is snapshot-only.

Exercise four-job/12-object bounds, immutable nonwrapping handle/op/job generations, permanent quarantine capacity exhaustion, token copy versus stale token, final-private release reset return bookkeeping, and facade free/start-failure safety.

Compile/exercise semantic mutants only after baseline succeeds; compile errors do not count as lifecycle safety detections. At least anchor transfer removed, retire-before-complete, retry failed prepare, retry failed complete, partial cohort free, constructor baseline completed manually, policy-after-zero and raw object free must be assertion-killed.
future_exact_SDK_compile_requirements: Separate source-only native TU opts into C++17+ shared pointer API macros before headers; compile against exact pinned Kernel.framework and actual toolchain. Assert factory return type/assignment ownership, no raw-pointer/OSPtr ABI assumption. No SDK execution of allocations implied.

Compile frozen lifecycle.c as C and provider TU as C++; wrap lifecycle.h in extern "C" without modifying it. Link the actual mixed-language objects and check unmangled bpl_init/claim/bind_metadata/inspect/quarantine/retire_private symbols; syntax-only C++ compilation is insufficient.

Compile real inTaskWithPhysicalMask(kernel_task,options,0x4000,0xfffffc000), prepare/complete, getLength/getCapacity/getPhysicalSegment(...MapperNone)/getBytesNoCopy and strong field reset calls against public headers; no private _wireCount/_flags/fPageSize/struct layout access.

Bind actual source/dependency/macro records and inspect ARM64 object/bundle imports against declared KPIs and retained kernel. Confirm shared PHY/PMGR writers/MMIO/IOMapper registration/IRQ/firmware/DMACommand transport are absent from translation/link units, not merely an untested branch.
Measure stack frames atO0/O2; registry/anchor/three large page buffers must be retained heap allocations rather than automatic48KiB arrays. Real table CPU/PA addresses must not be fixture literals.
SDK compile/host tests remain before any separately authorized private runtime allocation experiment. Hardware STOP cannot be cleared by this provider design or compile result.
remaining_nonclaims: No implementation, allocator call, SDK test, native descriptor acquired or preparation/completion executed by this report.
Private backing validation is neither hardware DART mapping nor physical/IRQ/firmware ownership. No exposure state or hardware-ready return exists.
Metadata core retirement releases reservations only; actual native reference reset is a later separately recorded step, not physical DMA drain proof.
Current PHY_NOT_READY/noP_PCIE_INIT/shared-writers-compiled-out/GPU HOLD and stopped network work remain unchanged.

Factory internal initialization/AutoPrepare may occur before any returned OSPtr can be anchored; before-zero validation applies to provider-owned zero/copy only. Constructor failure cleanup is native XNU responsibility, not an observed provider quarantine operation.
